```{r}
#| label: load-data
#| include: false
library(ggplot2)
library(ggrain)

h1Data <- read.csv("data/processed_data/practice_h1.csv")
h1Data$Sex_birth <- factor(h1Data$Sex_birth,
                           levels = c("Male", "Female", "Intersex"))
h2Data <- read.csv("data/processed_data/practice_h2.csv")
```

## Hypothesis 1

Sex at birth may predict gender equality attitudes. 

### Variables and descriptive statistics

- **Sex at birth (`Sex_birth`):** A categorical variable with three groups: Male, Female, and Intersex.
- **Gender equality attitudes (`gender_equa`):** Points allocated to gender equality. Higher values indicate greater equality.

```{r}
#| label: h1-descriptives
# Count respondents in each group.
table(h1Data$Sex_birth)

# Summarize gender equality points separately for each group.
by(h1Data$gender_equa, h1Data$Sex_birth, summary)
```

### Graph

@fig-gendequa shows the distribution of points by sex at birth. The half-violin shows the shape of the distribution, the box summarizes the median and quartiles, and the dots represent individual responses.

```{r}
#| label: fig-gendequa
#| fig-cap: "Points allocated to gender equality, by sex at birth."
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 5

ggplot(h1Data, aes(x = Sex_birth, y = gender_equa,
                   fill = Sex_birth)) +
  geom_rain(alpha = 0.5, point.args = list(alpha = 0.04, size = 0.6)) +
  labs(x = "Sex at birth", y = "Points allocated to gender equality") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "none")
```

## H2.

Intensity of love feelings may negatively predict the willingness to marry without love.

### Variables and descriptive statistics

- **Intensity of love feelings (`Love_how_much_1`):** A single item about how much one loves partner, applicable to only those in a relationship. Responses range from 1 to 100.
- **Willingness to marry without love (`Love_would_you_marry_1`):**  higher scores indicate greater willingness

This dataset includes respondents who were dating, in a committed relationship, or married.

```{r}
#| label: h2-descriptives
summary(h2Data[, c("Love_how_much_1", "Love_would_you_marry_1")])
```

### Graph

@fig-love shows the relationship between Intensity of love feelings and Willingness to marry without love. Points are jittered to make overlapping responses easier to see; the recorded scores are unchanged. The line summarizes the linear trend.

```{r}
#| label: fig-love
#| fig-cap: "Relationship between love feeling and willingness to marry without love."
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 5

ggplot(h2Data, aes(x = Love_how_much_1, y = Love_would_you_marry_1)) +
  geom_jitter(width = .12, height = .04, alpha = .04, size = .6) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm") +
  labs(x = "Intensity of love feelings",
       y = "Willingness to marry without love") +
  theme_minimal()
```

### Observed trend

```{r}
#| label: correlation
r <- cor(h2Data$Love_how_much_1, h2Data$Love_would_you_marry_1, use = "complete.obs")
round(r, 2)
```

The correlation was `{r} round(r, 2)`, indicating a weak negative association. Respondents who reported more love feeling tended to report lower willingness to marry without love.
